stem: A nurse explains why hand hygiene is part of a hospital's strategy against antimicrobial-resistant organisms. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.A: Hand hygiene reduces person-to-person transmission of germs, including antimicrobial-resistant organisms, and works alongside antimicrobial stewardship.
options.B: Hand hygiene directly reverses bacterial resistance genes after the organism contacts alcohol-based sanitizer.
options.C: Hand hygiene replaces the need for antimicrobial stewardship because transmission control alone prevents resistance from developing.
options.D: Hand hygiene has little effect on resistant-organism spread because MDRO transmission occurs independently of healthcare workers' hands.

rationale: A is correct. CDC states that cleaning hands reduces the spread of germs, including those resistant to antibiotics, and identifies healthcare workers' hands as an important route of MDRO transmission. Infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship address different parts of the resistance problem and are complementary. B is incorrect because hand hygiene removes or kills organisms; it does not genetically reverse resistance. C is incorrect because CDC separately emphasizes preventing spread and improving antibiotic/antifungal use. D contradicts CDC evidence that MDROs can be carried from one person to another via healthcare personnel's hands.
educational_objective: Explain that hand hygiene helps control antimicrobial resistance by interrupting transmission of resistant organisms, while antimicrobial stewardship separately addresses unnecessary or suboptimal antimicrobial exposure.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers; Epidemiology of MDROs; Antimicrobial Resistance: Causes and How It Spreads
source_version_date: CDC hand-hygiene page dated February 27, 2024; AR causes/spread page dated September 25, 2025; current pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Clinical Safety — Why it matters: hand hygiene reduces spread of germs, including those resistant to antibiotics. MDRO Epidemiology — Important concepts in transmission: epidemiologic evidence shows MDROs are carried person-to-person via healthcare personnel's hands and hand-hygiene adherence is an important control component. AR Causes and How It Spreads — prevention requires stopping spread, slowing development, improving antimicrobial use, and preventing infections.
source_claim_supported: Hand hygiene interrupts transmission of antimicrobial-resistant germs in healthcare settings and complements, rather than replaces, antimicrobial stewardship.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: perform hand hygiene and implement Standard Precautions to prevent transmission of infectious agents.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene and MDRO transmission
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw conceptual item to separate two mechanisms accurately: hand hygiene interrupts spread of resistant organisms, while stewardship addresses antimicrobial use. Removed any implication that handwashing changes bacterial genetics or independently prevents resistance development.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current CDC hand-hygiene, MDRO-transmission, and antimicrobial-resistance pages.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A states the source-supported transmission role and complementary stewardship relationship. B invents genetic reversal. C falsely makes hand hygiene a substitute for antimicrobial-use improvement. D denies a documented transmission route.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; transmission interruption plus complementary stewardship.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; sanitizers do not reverse resistance genes.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; HCP hands are an established MDRO transmission route.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A accurately separates infection-prevention and stewardship functions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address how hand hygiene relates to antimicrobial resistance.
audit_findings.blueprint: Hand hygiene and transmission prevention are core Safety/IPC constructs.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked CDC wording that sanitizer use itself does not create antimicrobial resistance and that hand hygiene prevents spread rather than directly changing susceptibility. No second answer or causal overstatement remained.
